one_liner: Payments, billing, and financial infrastructure APIs for internet businesses.

evidence.claim: The API is REST with resource-oriented URLs, form-encoded bodies, and JSON responses.
evidence.quote: The Stripe API is organized around REST. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts form-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses

evidence.claim: Primary authentication is API keys managed in the Stripe Dashboard.
evidence.quote: The Stripe API uses API keys to authenticate requests. You can view and manage your API keys in the Stripe Dashboard.

evidence.claim: Free self-serve test credentials: test-mode secret keys work in sandboxes immediately after account creation.
evidence.quote: Test mode secret keys start with `sk_test_` and have unrestricted access to their sandboxes.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 is also supported for apps acting on behalf of users.
evidence.quote: Your app can use one of three methods to authenticate requests to the Stripe API on behalf of your users.

evidence.claim: Stripe itself documents an official MCP server for AI agents.
evidence.quote: The Stripe Model Context Protocol (MCP) server provides a set of tools that AI agents can use to interact with the Stripe API and search our knowledge base

notes: Official MCP server documented at docs.stripe.com/mcp. Keys are sent as HTTP Basic username (curl -u sk_test_...:). Live mode offers restricted keys (rk_live_) with scoped permissions. Two API namespaces (v1 and v2); no bulk updates (one object per request). Live keys require account activation but no paid plan; Stripe charges per-transaction fees.
